newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Blue-chip firms lift Morocco's bourse 0.27 pct.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip firms lift Morocco's bourse 0.27 pct.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange closed 0.27 percent higher on Thursday with advances in most stocks despite low volumes traded on the official market, brokers said.
The bourse all-share index closed at 636.04 points from 634.32 points on Wednesday.
Morocco's biggest private conglomerate ONA Group was up five dirhams to 760 dirhams.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur rose six dirhams 588 dirhams with 8,834 shares changing hands.
Wafabank, rose nine dirhams to 799 dirhams
In the energy sector, oil refinery Samir took five dirhams to 355 dirhams.
Steel mill Sonasid was up five dirhams to 530 dirhams.
First and second tranche of privatisation bonds, issued in January and May 1996, gained respectively 12 and 10 dirhams to 1,357 and 1,170 dirhams.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, Morocco's second largest private group, dropped eight dirhams to 712 dirhams.
Banque Marocaine pour le Commerce et l'Industrie, dipped 10 dirhams to 480 dirhams.
Total traded volume on the official market was 31 million dirhams from 21.6 million dirhams, stockbrokers said.
On the over-the-counter (OTC) market, the volume was 70.3 million dirhams from 79.6 million dirhams over the previous session.
Cement firm Ciments de l'Oriental, which closed at 655 dirhams, had 46,003 shares exchanged on the OTC market, traders said.
